title: LifecycleEvent
description: Phase 2 lifecycle audit envelope emitted by AuditDispatcher.emit_lifecycle_event (packages/kernel-core/python/kernel_core/audit.py:120) v1.0.0. Governing artifacts: docs/work-packages/BOPEN-P1-001-EXECUTION-PLAN.md section 10.2 (Audit envelope), BOPEN-IDP-001 section 15, BOPEN-P2-001. This schema is written from the producer outward: every property below was observed on real events from all eight call sites (invitation, membership, IdP connection, SSO, identity linking, SCIM, context switching, delegation), which emit one uniform thirteen-key object with no variation. It is a SECOND audit envelope, distinct from audit-event.json and not a replacement for it. audit-event.json describes AuditDispatcher.dispatch (audit.py:70), which reports authorization decisions with `timestamp`, `actor_id` and `status` in {SUCCESS, DENIED, ERROR}. This envelope reports lifecycle outcomes with `occurred_at`, `actor_principal_id` and `outcome` in {success, deny, failure}. The two vocabularies name the same idea in different words and both producers are live; the divergence is recorded here rather than resolved, because audit-event.json is frozen, so a consumer reading both streams must map `status` and `outcome` onto a single domain itself. Note which side matches the specification: BOPEN-P1-001 section 10.2 specifies `event_version`, `occurred_at`, `causation_id`, `actor_principal_id`, `subject_type`/`subject_id` and `outcome` in {success, deny, failure} by those exact names, as does docs/06-contracts/events/event-envelope.md. This envelope implements that table; audit-event.json's field names appear in neither document. Two fields BOPEN-P1-001 section 10.2 does specify are absent from the producer and therefore from this schema: `policy_version` (specified as required for authorization events, which these are not) and `integrity_version`. They are recorded here as a known gap rather than declared, because a schema requiring a field the producer never writes is unsatisfiable by correct code. INV-P2-018 forbids credentials, assertions, authorization codes and tokens anywhere in this envelope; `metadata.propertyNames` enforces the key half of that prohibition.

event_id.description: Per-event identifier from uuid.uuid4(); unprefixed, unlike the mem_/inv_/grn_ identifiers minted by UuidIdentifierFactory elsewhere in Phase 2.

event_type.description: Closed catalogue. This enum is the exact contents of kernel_core.audit.PHASE2_EVENT_TYPES, which the producer checks before constructing the event and rejects with AuditContractError otherwise — so the closure is enforced twice, in code and here.

event_version.description: Envelope revision. The producer writes the literal 1 and has no branch that writes anything else; a second revision would be a new schema document rather than a widened enum here.

occurred_at.description: Emission instant from datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), so always carrying an explicit +00:00 offset. Named `occurred_at` and not `timestamp`; audit-event.json uses `timestamp` for the same concept.

correlation_id.description: Caller-supplied trace identifier, passed through unvalidated. Call sites supply either a request correlation id or, in ContextSwitchService, the idempotency key (context_service.py:350, 454) — so this value is not drawn from a single namespace across producers.

causation_id.description: Identifier of the command or prior event that caused this one. Always present as a key and, at the time of writing, always null: the parameter defaults to None at audit.py:131 and no caller in packages/kernel-core or services/platform-kernel passes it. Typed nullable rather than dropped because the producer always writes the key, and the causal chain it exists to carry is not yet threaded through.

actor_principal_id.description: Who acted. Not always a principal identifier despite the name: producers pass the sentinels 'anonymous' (unauthenticated invitation and SSO paths), 'security_control' (context revocation), 'expiry_scheduler' (batch expiry), 'scim_directory' and a bare directory_id (SCIM ingress). Left as a plain string because constraining it to a principal-id pattern would reject events the code legitimately emits today. audit-event.json calls this field `actor_id`.

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant boundary. The literal 'unknown' is emitted on paths that deny before a tenant is established (membership.py:523, idp_bridge.py:407), so this value is not always a resolvable tenant and must not be treated as one by a consumer.

subject_type.description: Kind of entity the event is about. Observed values across every call site: invitation, membership, connection, external_identity, scim_event, group, context, delegated_grant. Deliberately NOT an enum: unlike event_type and outcome, the producer performs no membership check on this argument, so a closed list here would be a constraint the code does not hold and could reject a legitimate new subject kind before anyone noticed the schema had drifted from the producer.

subject_id.description: Identifier of the subject entity. Denial paths substitute the sentinels 'unknown' and 'none' when the subject could not be resolved (membership.py:792, context_service.py:354, idp_bridge.py:412), so this is not always a dereferenceable identifier.

outcome.description: Lifecycle result. The producer rejects anything outside this set with AuditContractError (audit.py:141), and the set is exactly the one BOPEN-P1-001 section 10.2 specifies for this field. 'failure' is declared and reachable through emit_lifecycle_event but is emitted by no Phase 2 call site: every producer passes 'success' or 'deny'. Distinct in both spelling and membership from audit-event.json's `status` enum {SUCCESS, DENIED, ERROR}, which no governing document names.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable justification. Sourced from three unrelated namespaces: literals at the call site (INVITATION_ISSUED, CONTEXT_ISSUED, GRANT_REVOKED), KernelError.code on denial paths, and caller-supplied TransitionCommand.reason_code validated against the transition matrix. No single vocabulary governs it, so it is unconstrained beyond non-emptiness. Note that audit-event.json has no reason property at all, while AuditDispatcher.dispatch emits one.

metadata.description: Bounded per-event detail. Always present, sometimes empty. Observed value types are string, integer, null and array-of-string; no nested object appears at any call site, but none is forbidden, so this stays open rather than pretending to a flatness the producer does not enforce.

propertyNames.description: INV-P2-018, expressed as far as JSON Schema can express it. This mirrors kernel_core.audit.PROHIBITED_METADATA_KEYS exactly. The producer's check is stricter in two ways this schema cannot reproduce: it lowercases the key before comparing, so it also catches 'Password' and 'AUTHORIZATION'; and it scans string VALUES for JWT-shaped and SAML-shaped content, which no keyword here can do. The schema is therefore strictly weaker than the producer — the safe direction, since it can never reject an event the producer legitimately allowed.
